title: Build the scorecard generator and wire it into BENCHMARKS.md
summary: benchmarks/common/scorecard.py reads pytest-benchmark/Locust output, BM-18's LongMemEval results, and AGQ-2/3/4's agent-quality results, computes UNI-2's composite score, and appends a scorecard section to BENCHMARKS.md plus a CI artifact.
description:
Implement `benchmarks/common/scorecard.py`: a report generator that reads the three sub-score sources — pytest-benchmark's JSON output (EPIC-14/15) compared against EPIC-19's BM-27 committed baselines, EPIC-16's BM-18 LongMemEval results, and EPIC-21's AGQ-2/AGQ-3/AGQ-4 agent-quality results — applies UNI-2's normalization and weighting, and renders a single Markdown scorecard section (composite score, three sub-scores with their own numbers, and a one-line 'why' for any sub-score below its threshold). Append this section to BENCHMARKS.md as part of EPIC-19's BM-26 rewrite structure (extend, don't compete with, that document's existing per-suite sections), and add the scorecard as a CI artifact upload on EPIC-17's nightly Tier 2 job (the only tier where all three sub-score inputs — including the non-deterministic LLM-judged ones — are actually produced in the same run).

Historical-record discipline matches BM-26: if any of the three source runs is missing or stale (e.g. AGQ suite hasn't run yet), the scorecard must say so explicitly per sub-score rather than silently omitting it or defaulting it to zero — a missing sub-score is a different finding than a zero score and must not be conflated.

**Acceptance criteria:**
- `scorecard.py` produces a deterministic Markdown table given fixed input JSON fixtures (unit-testable without a live Db2 instance or LLM judge).
- BENCHMARKS.md scorecard section renders correctly end-to-end on a real nightly Tier 2 run.
- Missing/stale sub-score inputs are surfaced, not silently zeroed.
- Config-driven weights from UNI-2 are respected (changing the weights file changes the composite without a code change).

**Definition of Done:**
- Unit tests for `scorecard.py` (fixture-based, per the acceptance criteria above) pass in the normal test suite, not gated on live Db2.
- One real end-to-end scorecard generated and committed to BENCHMARKS.md as the first published composite score.
- Depends on UNI-2 (the formula) and EPIC-21's AGQ-5 (a real agent-quality sub-score to consume) and EPIC-19's BM-26/BM-27 (the document structure and baselines this appends to/compares against).
